source_review.notes: Checked Lamport's original multiprocess correctness and liveness papers, Alpern-Schneider's defining-liveness DOI record, current 2026 Lamport book and fairness note, Herlihy et al.'s second-edition publisher record, and durable Lynch, Manna-Pnueli, and Dijkstra foundations. Current-source claims are dated and progress terminology is bounded to declared models.

evidence: Checked infinite behavior, finite prefix, extension-set, safety, liveness, invariant, temporal, fairness, and progress notation.
Checked always/eventually, stabilization, recurrence, and response distinctions.
Checked that progress conditions identify system-wide versus per-operation beneficiaries.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation is lightweight, defined before use, and does not assume a particular temporal-logic tool.

evidence: Enumerated all 2^4=16 length-four scheduler choice words.
Confirmed zero mutual-exclusion violations in the synthetic model.
Confirmed exactly two schedules complete both clients and fourteen remain incomplete at the bound.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Incomplete finite prefixes are explicitly not counted as liveness violations.

evidence: Re-derived invariant proof obligations Init implies I and I-and-Next implies next-I.
Checked finite-bad-prefix safety and extension-based liveness definitions.
Checked ranking-function reasoning over a well-founded order and transitive composition of leads-to obligations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Every liveness derivation retains fairness, enabledness, and environment premises.

evidence: Reviewed stuttering, continuous and intermittent enabledness, unfair cycles, deadlock, livelock, starvation, cancellation, timeout, and permanent dependency failure.
Reviewed global versus per-operation completion, formal steps versus wall time, and weak versus strong fairness.
Reviewed priority starvation, owner descheduling, crash recovery, overload, retry overlap, and aggregate metrics hiding one stuck operation.
Reviewed railway and clinical-alarm transfers for safety, human factors, regulatory authority, and model fidelity.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-consequence cases require actual named authorized review and do not inherit approval from formal evidence.

evidence: Traced subject, trigger, response, quantification, and observation through every requirement pattern.
Confirmed history-sensitive safety uses monitor state and all transition kinds require preservation.
Confirmed fairness attaches to actions and environment recovery remains an assumption.
Confirmed cancellation and timeout do not silently weaken effect safety.
invariant_checking.notes: Safety, liveness, progress, deadline, and statistical claims remain separate throughout.

evidence: Reviewed induction structure for state invariants.
Reviewed why a finite prefix cannot refute pure liveness but can refute a deadline.
Reviewed ranking and leads-to proof outlines with fairness and interference obligations.
Reviewed counterexamples showing mutual exclusion without entry and global progress with individual starvation.
proof_review.notes: The chapter does not present bounded exploration as an infinite theorem.

evidence: Audited uses of safety, liveness, eventually, always, fair, deadlock-free, lock-free, wait-free, prove, and guarantee.
Confirmed algorithmic progress is separated from scheduler and wall-clock behavior.
Confirmed every formal claim names or preserves its model assumptions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No timeout, load test, bounded run, aggregate SLO, or atomic operation is mislabeled as universal progress.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-004/report.json records deterministic finite execution for finite-safety-progress-check.
The chapter limits its result to sixteen length-four synthetic schedules.
Monitoring, load tests, model checking, systematic scheduling, invariants, and liveness proofs are separate evidence layers.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production fairness, latency, starvation freedom, clinical safety, railway safety, regulatory approval, or external review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed behavior, prefix, safety, invariant, liveness, response, persistence, recurrence, termination, deadline, deadlock, livelock, starvation, weak/strong fairness, blocking, obstruction-free, lock-free, wait-free, scheduler steps, and wall time as distinct concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed requirement decomposition, monitor construction, invariant preservation, ranking functions, cycle search, schedule control, virtual time, replay, cancellation, timeout, SLOs, oldest-item monitoring, and deployment-assumption monitoring. Internal concurrency-practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from bad prefixes and invariants through infinite behaviors, fairness, progress hierarchy, well-founded arguments, bounded evidence, monitoring, and high-consequence review. Ten examples and five complete exercises cover classification, proof design, monitoring, comparison, and unfamiliar transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, concurrency, model-checking, scheduler, operating-system, hardware, reliability, railway, clinical-safety, human-factors, cybersecurity, quality, regulatory, independent-assurance, or practitioner review is claimed.
